question: Can merged context-scoped managed graph winners coexist with SGLang legacy startup/eager winners, persist across fresh processes, and serve a retained decode graph after scope exit?
scope: Bounded lifecycle qualification through one actual dense FP8 SGLang model; no ranking or performance comparison.

model.weights: Real serialized checkpoint, with file hashes bound before execution; no dummy weights or predicate overrides.

environment.flashinfer: Base 27c62fdf0ab1cd4014df8a15b66a975541fda83c plus the qualified explicit-FP8 descriptor and benchmark-validation overlays; reuse exact prior native GEMM. This is not a stock-release claim. The #7521 debug guard is not overlaid.

protocol.cold: Fresh isolated legacy and managed roots; run actual SGLang startup and graph-region tuning on the real prepared decode closure.
protocol.warm: Fresh process and container with the identical cold legacy and graph cache bytes, same paths, checkpoint, source, controls, policy and hardware; require zero profiling.
prepared_forward_sequence: Actual completed legacy startup outside any v2 scope.
Legacy report-only prepared decode forward: genuine hits, record keys/winners/files/controls.
Strict replay with a separate empty managed root and graph policy must raise on the first actual miss despite populated legacy winners, perform zero profiling/publication and restore legacy state.
One prepared decode forward in the identified graph tuning context.
One strict replay context around the unchanged backend capture routine: its two warmups are preflight, followed by actual CUDA graph capture.
Exit the graph scope, then repeat legacy prepared forward and compare actual winners and legacy file bytes/state.
Run the fresh-prefix original/changed/restored numerical comparisons outside identified graph scopes.
protocol.prepared_forward_reset: Synchronize and invoke the supplied attention post_warmup_hook after every added attempt, including expected strict miss; retain the backend original warmups/reset hooks.

graph_tuning_context.cache_root: dedicated managed root, stable across both processes

graph_capture_context.cache_root: same managed root as graph tuning

protocol.inherited_controls: Do not override skip_ops, tuning_buckets, round_up or profiler settings. Explicit graph policy is only the separately identified scope under test; no optimal-policy claim.
protocol.capture_context_placement: Resolve/hydrate the managed scope before original capture_one so filesystem/store setup occurs before actual CUDA capture.
protocol.numerics: Fresh identical prefixes and KV state for each eager/retained-graph arm; original, changed and restored decode token. Clone outputs; poison retained graph output before replay; require original graph and output owner unchanged, real replay, no new profiling.
numerical_additional_checks: restored input restores output within fixed tolerance
protocol.source_freeze: Commit and push worker, launcher, analyzer, exact model manifest and protocol before GPU execution. Preserve failed setup/admission attempts with their original source attribution. Do not adapt samples or thresholds after observations.

validity_requirements: Actual ModelRunner and real serialized ModelOpt FP8 checkpoint with 128 eligible FlashInfer linear layers; no predicate overrides or dummy weights.
One ordinary batch-one full decode graph, two existing warmups and actual capture distinguished by CUDA capture state.
Legacy before/after and numerical eager reports remain legacy identity with genuine same winners; cached -1 is a hit only when lookup status says hit.
Empty identified-store strict control cannot fall through to legacy/bundled/default selection; expected exception, one miss, no profiling/publication and restored controls.
Graph tuning and strict preflight/capture share a nonlegacy managed root/policy identity and matching stored profiling provenance; no nested v2 or ambient store attachment.
Scope exit restores legacy active partition, controls and v1 bytes; managed registry/identified partitions may persist intentionally.
No delegated protocol consumers in observed region; these require separate qualification.
Exact source, helper, container, checkpoint, native provider and persisted cache provenance bound to frozen execution commit.
Numerics use actual retained graph after scope exit with output freshness and changed/restored inputs; no retuning or recapture.
coverage_requirements: Cold legacy startup and graph tuning each profile actual candidates and publish their own winners.
All 128 expected FP8 selections in each of the two existing warmups and actual capture are strict hits in the same graph identity, with zero misses/skips/dropped records.
Fresh warm process loads exact cold legacy and managed winner files and performs zero profiling during startup, graph tuning, capture and serving.
Managed winner files survive scope exit and are unchanged by capture/serving/warm reuse.
Legacy actual eager selections, live cache, controls and v1 files survive graph tuning/scope exit unchanged.
All six eager-versus-retained-graph numerical comparisons pass the frozen finite/allclose/argmax gates, changed inputs change results and restored inputs restore results.
decision_rule: Preserve valid lifecycle misses, reprofile, restoration or numerical failures as findings; do not treat them as discardable samples. Stop after one cold/fresh-warm pair, or an admission failure. Repair only demonstrated harness/setup defects under a new frozen source/attempt without deleting prior evidence. A pass qualifies this bounded lifecycle only and does not automatically authorize a production policy/ownership change.
limits: One H100 NVL, one actual dense FP8 model, TP1, batch-one full decode and one cold/fresh-warm pair.
Qualified pinned source overlays, not an unmodified release or latest-main claim.
No selection-quality, profiling-objective superiority, latency, throughput or general model-quality claim.
Cache selection reports do not prove every backend physical kernel identity; graph replay does not perform Python tactic lookup.
No TP/EP, concurrent tuning/stores, prefill graphs, speculative decoding or MegaMoE qualification.
Production SGLang startup policy and v1 persistence remain unchanged; no production code edits, CI triggers, external messages or PR.
Ranking/measurement-causality investigation remains paused for owner feedback; old scoped-cache prototype remains parked.
